content.text: {"primary_meaning":"A “new name” most commonly symbolizes a new, God-given identity and status—often associated with transformation, belonging to God, vindication, and a new vocation or destiny.","primary_basis":["Isaiah 62:2–4 — restored Zion receives a new name from the LORD, marking vindication and changed status.","Revelation 2:17 — the conqueror receives a white stone bearing a new name known only to its recipient.","Revelation 3:12 — Christ writes on the conqueror the names of God, the New Jerusalem, and Christ’s own new name, signifying belonging and eschatological identity.","Genesis 17:5, 15 — Abram and Sarai become Abraham and Sarah in connection with covenant promises.","Genesis 32:28; 35:10 — Jacob is renamed Israel after his encounter with God.","John 1:42; Matthew 16:17–18 — Simon is called Cephas/Peter in connection with calling and vocation.","Isaiah 56:5 — God promises the faithful an everlasting “name,” expressing honored and enduring standing."] ,"alternatives":[{"meaning":"A uniquely personal, secret eschatological name expressing intimate communion between Christ and each victorious believer.","basis":["Revelation 2:17 emphasizes that no one knows the name except the one who receives it."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"A corporate designation for restored Zion, Jerusalem, or the covenant people, rather than primarily an individual identity.","basis":["Isaiah 62:2–4 addresses Zion/Jerusalem collectively.","Revelation 3:12 associates believers with the name of the New Jerusalem."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"A mark of divine ownership, allegiance, citizenship, and protection, comparable to bearing God’s name or seal.","basis":["Revelation 3:12 places divine and civic names upon the conqueror.","Revelation 7:3–4 and 14:1 depict God’s servants bearing the divine name or seal.","Revelation 22:4 says God’s name will be on the servants’ foreheads."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"A revelation of Christ’s own previously hidden or newly manifested identity and authority, rather than a renamed identity given to the believer.","basis":["Revelation 3:12 refers specifically to Christ’s “new name.”","Revelation 19:12 describes Christ as having a name known only to himself, while Revelation 19:16 presents his royal title."],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"A literal replacement name that redeemed individuals will use in the age to come.","basis":["A literal reading of Revelation 2:17 and analogies with biblical renaming narratives."],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is broad consensus on the general symbolism of a divinely bestowed, transformed identity or status. There is no settled consensus on the precise content of the “new name” in Revelation 2:17 or whether it is the believer’s personal name, Christ’s name, a designation of belonging, or a combination of these ideas."}
